Chechelnyk Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Chechelnyk, believed founded in the 17th century, saw Jewish settlement soon after, though the community suffered repeated attacks from Khmelnytsky's followers, Cossacks, and Haidamakas across the 17th and 18th centuries. The Great Synagogue, built in the late 18th century, survives today as picturesque ruins visible in the town. By 1897, Jews comprised more than 40 percent of the population (3,388 of 7,993), though poverty was common, with no charitable organizations and 23 small chadarim serving 367 boys. Following the July 1941 German capture and inclusion in the Transnistria Governorate, a ghetto held 600-800 local Jews plus over 1,000 more from Bessarabia and Bukovina, with many dying of disease, starvation, and forced labor before aid from Bucharest arrived in January 1943. This cemetery, situated next to the Catholic cemetery, holds around 5,000 graves, its oldest surviving matzevot dating to the early 19th century; Jewish visitors still come to the site every year.
